newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican same-day Cetes rate pare gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexican same-day Cetes rate pare gains at close.

text.p: Mexican same-day Cetes rates on Thursday ended five basis points up at 21.30 percent, coming off earlier highs and still pressured by fears ahead of closely contested midterm elections on July 6.
"We're still seeing upward pressure. There's a lot of speculation because of the elections," a trader said. Others said foreigners were reluctant to come into the market ahead of the elections.

The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) is facing a tough fight to retain its 68-year control of the lower house of Congress, according to opinion polls. It is also expected to lose the key race for Mexico City mayor.
Analysts said the slight respite for same-day paper came ahead a brief flurry of enthusiasm on the back of a strong rally in the stock market. But it was not expected to last.
"There are month-end and quarter-end liquidity pressures, which always affect rates," a trader said.

Rates fluctuated between 20.90 percent and 21.85 percent during the day, and traders also kept a wary eye on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond, whose yield climbed to 6.78 percent from 6.74 at Wednesday's close.
Bank paper was up 90 basis points at 23 percent.
